newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ROMARIO CHANGES MIND ABOUT VALENCIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO CHANGES MIND ABOUT VALENCIA.

text.p: Brazilian international striker Romario has changed his mind and will play for Valencia next season after all, a Spanish newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Romario, who has been on loan to Brazilian club Flamengo, had previously suggested that he would not return to Spain because he wanted to stay in Brazil to be close to his sons.
"I never thought I would leave Flamengo but I am a professional," Romario was quoted as saying in Spanish sports daily Marca. "The best thing now is for me to go and succeed with my Spanish club."
Romario did not say what had made him change his mind but Flamengo president Kleber Leite is believed to have persuaded him to fulfil his contract obligations.

Leite had talks with Valencia president Francisco Roig on Monday about Romario returning to the Brazilian club after the 1998 World Cup. Valencia loaned him to Flamengo for one year at the start of last season.
Romario was left out of the Brazil squad announced on Tuesday for a tour of the Far East in August.
